newsitem.title: FRANCE: French car sales rise 29.4 pct in August - CCFA.
newsitem.headline: French car sales rise 29.4 pct in August - CCFA.

text.p: New car sales in France rose 29.4 percent in August from year-earlier levels to 172,400, the French carmakers committee CCFA said. On a basis of comparable days, the rise was 35.5 percent, it said in a statement.
PSA Peugeot Citroen car sales in France rose 25.6 percent last month from August 1995 levels, while Renault SA sales climbed 29.3 percent.
Sales of foreign cars in France rose 31.7 percent from year-earlier levels for a combined market share of 47.7 percent.
In the first eight months of 1995, car sales totalled 1.44 million units, up 7.4 percent from the year-earlier period.
French car makers held 52.3 percent of the domestic market in August and 55.4 percent for the eight-month period.

New car sales in France in July totalled 234,900.
Totals may not add up because PSA or Renault figures do not include vehicles sold by niche producers or because of rounding.
The August rise partly reflects a surge in demand ahead of the expiry at the end of September of a state rebate scheme, the CCFA said. The rebate plan was tied to 30 percent of the August orders.
The increase is also due to the weak sales in August 1995 following the expiry on June 30, 1995, of a previous incentive scheme.
